subject.title: [Feature]: Feishu Group Chat SubAgents for User-Specific Skills and Memory

question: Should Feishu group-chat isolation be solved with sender-scoped sessions and memory namespaces, automatic per-user group subagents, or a Feishu plugin experiment before any core or SDK contract is added?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the requested behavior changes cross-user memory, skills, config, lifecycle, quota, and message-routing boundaries that automation cannot choose safely.

options.title: Design The Feishu Isolation Seam First
options.body: Use the current sender/topic session and subagent binding primitives as inputs, define memory/config/lifecycle/security boundaries, and then implement the approved seam.

options.title: Prototype In The Feishu Plugin
options.body: Validate routing, cleanup, quotas, shared/private memory, and admin controls inside the Feishu plugin before promoting any generic SDK or core contract.

options.title: Move to external plugin experiment
options.body: Ask interested teams to prototype the orchestration outside core or in ClawHub until a missing plugin API is proven.

recommendation.title: Design The Feishu Isolation Seam First
recommendation.body: Use the current sender/topic session and subagent binding primitives as inputs, define memory/config/lifecycle/security boundaries, and then implement the approved seam.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision is primarily Feishu plugin product/security behavior, and the package metadata names this handle as the community maintainer.
